newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Former Bangladesh ruler Ershad pledges democracy.
newsitem.headline: Former Bangladesh ruler Ershad pledges democracy.

text.p: Former Bangladesh president Hossain Mohammad Ershad, freed from jail a week ago, said on Thursday he would devote the rest of his political career to developing sustainable democracy in the country.
"I have resumed my political career and will use it to establish truly democratic rule," he told tens of thousands of followers in the northern town of Syedpur.
"I was forced to waste six of my years in prison as a result of political vengeance...but now I will work for the people only," Ershad said in a choked voice.
He had left Dhaka for Syedpur on Thursday on way to his ancestral home in the northern district of Rangpur.
He is scheduled to address a public rally in Rangpur on Friday afternoon.
On Thursday, the small airport at Syedpur was crowded with well-wishers, many of whom chanted "Long live Ershad" and "Cheers for the hero", while others danced to the beat of drums.
Witnesses said tens of thousands of people, including children dressed in colourful tribal clothes, lined the 25 km (15 miles) highway from Syedpur to Rangpur to greet Ershad.
The former president was freed from Dhaka Central Jail on January 9, a day after he was granted bail by the Supreme Court on the last of a series of corruption charges against him.
The former army chief of staff, who seized power in a bloodless coup in 1982 and was toppled in a popular uprising in December 1990, faced 19 charges of corruption and misuse of power.

Ershad's Jatiya Party supported Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina's Awami League in its bid to form a government after a general election in June. Ershad fought the election from jail and was elected member of parliament.
